Keep all three options in the notebook: EvalautionClient, OnDemandEvaalutionDatasetRunner as well as BatchEvalaution. Include this differentiator in the markdown:
The SDK ships two dataset runners with different orchestration models — choosing the right one matters.

| | OnDemandEvaluationDatasetRunner | BatchEvaluationRunner |
|---|---|---|
| **Where evaluation runs** | Client-side: invoke → wait → collect spans → call Evaluate API, all in one `run()` call | Service-side: invoke → wait → `StartBatchEvaluation` → poll `GetBatchEvaluation` |
| **Results** | Per-scenario, per-evaluator detail immediately in the response object | Aggregate `averageScore` per evaluator; per-session detail in CloudWatch |
| **Best for** | Dev-time iteration, CI/CD pipelines, small datasets, debugging individual scenarios | Baseline measurement, large datasets, pre/post comparison across many sessions |
| **Evaluator support** | All built-ins + custom evaluators; handles session/trace/tool-call levels automatically | All built-ins; service caps at 500 sessions per job |
| **Phase count** | 3 phases: Invoke → Wait → Evaluate | 4 phases: Invoke → Wait → Submit → Poll |

Both notebooks demonstrate the same customer support use case but with different memory setup approaches:

**customer-support.ipynb (Simpler approach):**

- Uses MemoryClient directly for memory creation
- Uses built-in strategies: StrategyType.USER_PREFERENCE and StrategyType.SEMANTIC
- No IAM execution role required
- Simpler configuration - just specify strategy types
- Best for: Quick prototyping and standard use cases

**customer-support-memory-manager.ipynb (Advanced approach):**

- Uses MemoryManager from the starter toolkit for memory creation
- Uses custom strategies: CustomUserPreferenceStrategy and CustomSemanticStrategy
- Requires IAM execution role (memory_execution_role_arn) for custom model invocation
- Advanced configuration with ExtractionConfig and ConsolidationConfig
- Allows specifying custom models for extraction and consolidation (e.g., different Claude models)
- Best for: Production use cases requiring fine-tuned control over memory extraction

**Both notebooks use:**

- MemorySessionManager and MemorySession for session-based operations
- Same agent hooks and memory retrieval patterns
- Same customer support scenario and tools

The key difference is in the **memory resource creation step** - one uses built-in strategies (simpler), the other uses custom strategies with model configuration (more control).
